title: BACK↔BIZ-001: Cloud OpEx vs Business Budget + API Scalability/Monetization Inputs
description: The Backend/Cloud Engineer provides cloud operational-cost estimates (compute, storage, data transfer, and IoT — Internet of Things — platform fees per device per month), an API (Application Programming Interface) infrastructure scalability assessment and cost-scaling curve, and cloud vendor contract terms with volume-discount availability; the Business Consultant provides the cloud platform-selection business rationale (cost, vendor lock-in risk, GTM — Go-to-Market — partner alignment), API monetization requirements derived from the data strategy, and the device-connectivity cost budget from the unit-economics model. Grounded in BACKEND_CLOUD_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.11 and BUSINESS_CONSULTANT_SKILL §6.6. Cloud-platform selection outside the approved stack is an Architect/ADR decision; the Business Consultant supplies rationale only — the binding choice is ratified via ADR.

cloud_cost_package.description: BACK→BIZ: per-device-month OpEx, API scalability + cost curve, vendor terms.

opex_per_device_month.description: Operational cost components per device per month; each carries currency and a per-device/month unit.

cost_scaling_curve.description: Cost vs fleet-size points; each carries a device-count and a cost with units.

business_cloud_inputs.description: BIZ→BACK: platform-selection rationale, API monetization requirements, device-connectivity cost budget.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Routine cloud-cost reporting and unit-economics input exchange is agent-autonomous (architecture design stage; quarterly cloud cost review; scaling decision points). A cloud OpEx projection over the device-connectivity cost budget is surfaced as a unit-economics trade; a cloud-platform change outside the approved stack escalates to an Architect/ADR decision.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER + CALENDAR (at architecture design stage; quarterly cloud cost review; at scaling decision points)
confirm_conditions: every cloud-cost component carries value, currency, and a per-device/month (or per-month) unit
the cost-scaling curve ties cost to an explicit device-count unit (e.g., devices)
the device-connectivity cost budget is stated with units for comparison against OpEx
vendor terms and volume-discount availability are reported where a scaling decision depends on them
reject_conditions: a cloud-cost or budget quantity emitted without a unit (units rule §3.10)
projected OpEx over the device-connectivity cost budget presented as within unit economics without flagging the trade (Honesty Over Polish §10.3)
a cloud-platform selection outside the approved stack treated as decided here without an ADR (Architect decision)
counter_conditions: API monetization requirements imply an architecture change beyond the contracted API surface — request an ADR / Architect review before commitment
the cost-scaling curve is requested beyond the validated fleet ceiling (SCALE-1 50,000 devices) — request load validation before quoting
